A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 38 pages in each version, including Appendices A–F, equations, ten figures, and seven tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data experiments, document and cell classification results, and appendix robustness and MNIST evaluations. Some baseline scores are explicitly attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and results in Section 5 and the appendices, alongside explicitly attributed baseline scores.

M1.justification: The diffusion embedding, HD-LCA construction, binary-tree decoding, and TWD computation are unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 retain their procedures; Algorithm 2's function-name edit is cosmetic.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic hierarchical data, BBCSPORT, TWITTER, CLASSIC, AMAZON, Zeisel, CBMC, and MNIST. The later main-text reference to non-hierarchical applications points to the existing Appendix E.4 experiment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including TWD and graph/clustering methods, WMD/GMD, alternative hyperbolic embeddings, and ED/OT-ED comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same sample sizes, 70/30 splits, preprocessing, kNN settings, and parameter searches. Appendix evaluation procedures are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the toy recovery and runtime analyses, initial-distance and tree-construction ablations, alternative embeddings, curvature sensitivity, Gaussian-noise robustness, and non-hierarchical MNIST evaluation. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The five-run information and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix D.1. The figures retain the same uncertainty displays.

E6.justification: All 46 numerical result rows across Tables 1 and 3–7 match, and the result figures retain their graphical content. For example, Table 1 reports the same proposed-method accuracies of 99.8±0.1 on synthetic data and 89.1±0.4 on Zeisel.

T1.justification: Section 3 revises the formal tree setup from m vertices with an m-by-m weight matrix to a vertex set V with m leaves and a |V|-by-|V| matrix, distinguishing leaves from all vertices. The TWD formula, main propositions and theorems, and Appendix C proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about latent-feature hierarchy recovery, hyperbolic tree decoding, computational efficiency, and empirical advantages.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged, including the probability-simplex restriction and qualifications concerning non-hierarchical data. The added main-text applicability remark summarizes the existing Appendix E.4 discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds a Reproducibility Statement with a code-repository link and a pointer to Appendix D. The implementation settings and hardware information were already documented in v2; the PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness.

R1.justification: Appendices A.2 and B add background citations to Lin et al. (2024), Lin et al. (2025), and Mendelman and Talmon (2025). These modestly extend the literature coverage without changing the paper's central positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds Ethics and Reproducibility Statements, expands affiliations and acknowledgments, numbers appendix remarks, and makes limited prose edits. Most wording and the scientific section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The manuscript is retypeset throughout in ICLR format, changing text width, typography, headers, display sizes, and figure/table placement. All ten figures and seven tables are retained; Figure 7 moves from page 32 to 33 and Table 7 from page 37 to 38 without content changes.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility documentation through the corrected vertex-versus-leaf setup in Section 3 and the new code-access statement. Added references provide limited contextual benefit. The extensive reformatting leaves the methods, proofs, and empirical evidence essentially unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
